open_points.text: | A5 | rules 1 to 4, token and listening address | `deliverer_api` |
open_points.question: Does `deliverer_api` generate and persist the token as part of owning A5 rule 2, or does an installation/deployment actor own generation while `deliverer_api` only reads and validates the token file?
options: `deliverer_api` generates and writes the token file
an installation or deployment actor generates and writes it; `deliverer_api` only reads and validates it
open_points.default_guess: An installation or deployment actor generates and writes the token; `deliverer_api` only reads and validates it, matching its explicit ownership list and candidate capabilities.

witness.initial: A new installation has no token file.
events: The deployment actor starts the service without first provisioning a token.
outcomes: Because `deliverer_api` owns all of A5 rule 2, it generates the 32 random bytes and creates the token file, then starts.
Because `deliverer_api` owns only reading, start refusal and comparison, startup fails until an external actor creates the token file.
witness.observer: the deployment operator and the calling flow

open_points.subject: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
open_points.text: when what remains has fewer characters than the imported `TOKEN_MIN_LENGTH` constant or any character that is not visible ASCII (`!` to `~`)
open_points.question: Must the token read from the file have exactly the specified 43-character URL-safe Base64 form, or may any visible-ASCII token of at least `TOKEN_MIN_LENGTH` characters start the service?
options: accept any visible-ASCII token with at least 32 characters
open_points.default_guess: Accept any visible-ASCII token of at least 32 characters, while treating the 43-character URL-safe Base64 form as the required generation procedure.

witness.initial: The token file is a regular mode-0600 file containing 32 visible ASCII exclamation marks.
events: A caller presents those 32 characters in the Bearer header.
outcomes: Startup is refused because the token is not the specified 43-character URL-safe Base64 value.
Startup succeeds and the request authenticates because the trimmed token meets the stated minimum-length and visible-ASCII checks.
